messages.author: 617e83c95fc0d514
messages.subject: transforming covariates for pcount
parts:
Dear unmarked users.
Please advise me on how to transform my categorical covariates for use in pcount.

I am trying to investigate the variability of abundance among 60 sites, and I have 3 habitats types (wooded grassland, open grassland and riverine forest); I have riverbank type (earth, sand, and nriver); water body type (river, stream, village); presence/absence of nests; presence/absence of water at site. etc.

How can I transform or standardize such? Or do I need to all anyway?

Carol

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] transforming covariates for pcount
parts:
hi Carol,
 
 you should not have to standardize categorical covariates. If they are recognized as type "factor" in a dataframe then everything should work out fine when you fit models with pcount().
 
pcount will create a set of dummy variables to fit the model (just as lm() or glm() do also).  If you are unfamiliar with the basic ideas, you can read some of the lm or glm documentation/examples to understand the general principles.
 
regards,
andy
